calls.title: Custom LLM Experiment
calls.text: {"summary": "This custom LLM experiment involved training a tiny word-level language model, Karpathy's nanoGPT, from scratch on CPU. Two experiments were conducted, one using a starter corpus and one expanded with teaching files on grammar, opposites, and spatial relations.", "details": [{"text": "The model is a tiny word-level language model: Karpathy's nanoGPT (2 blocks, 4 heads, 64-number embeddings, 48-token context), trained from scratch on CPU.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "Two experiments were run with identical settings: the supplied starter corpus, then the starter corpus plus my own teaching files for grammar, opposites, and spatial relations.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "The model continues short sentences; it is not a chatbot.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "Experiment 1 used the starter corpus, while Experiment 2 used the starter corpus plus three plain-text files.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "The teaching files included passages on grammar, opposites, and spatial relations.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "Training steps were set to 3,000, which is enough practice for a model this small to learn the sentence patterns.", "section": "S3"}, {"text": "The learning rate was set to 0.001, which is large enough to make progress within 3,000 steps and small enough to avoid overshooting.", "section": "S3"}, {"text": "The fixed settings across both experiments included seed 42, model size, batch size, steps, learning rate, the 48-case eval suite, and the eval generation settings.", "section": "S4"}]}

calls.title: Custom LLM Training Results
calls.text: {"summary": "This section compares the results of Custom LLM Training Experiments 1 and 2 based on temperature settings. The comparison shows how different temperature values affect the generated output for the same trained weights and starting token.", "details": [{"text": "Same trained weights, same starting token and sampling seed; only the temperature differs.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "In Experiment 1, temperature barely mattered.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "0.8 and 1.2 gave identical samples in Experiment 1.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "At temperature 0.3 in Experiment 1, one sample swapped a single word (deposit → investment) and one became a different sentence entirely.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "In Experiment 2, 1.2 produced a garbled line, because a 481-word vocabulary has more low-probability tail to sample from.", "section": "S2"}, {"text": "Temperature changes the odds before the pick. Low makes the top word win more, high spreads it out. The weights never change.", "section": "S2"}]}

calls.title: Custom LLM Evaluation
calls.text: {"summary": "This document details a custom LLM experiment involving fixed language evaluations across different corpus stages. The evaluation scoring system is based on the highest probability among four choices, and it tracks success rates across various categories.", "details": [{"text": "The scoring rule states that only the prefix goes into the model, with no answer choices or key.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "A case scores 1 if the correct word has the highest probability among its four choices, and ties result in a score of 0.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "Any unknown prompt or answer word marks the case as `out_of_vocabulary`, which counts as 0 in the all-case rate.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "A separate free continuation is generated for every case with a temperature of 0.8, per-case seed, and 24 tokens, but it is not scored.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "The coverage rose from 24/48 to 26/48 because my files made 1 opposites case and 1 spatial case scorable.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "Training cannot change coverage; only corpus text can.", "section": "S1"}, {"text": "The model learned templates, not language, with 16/16 success on familiar patterns, but new wording was mostly guessing in Experiment 1.", "section": "S2"}]}
